problem: Embodied navigation agents usually learn visual representations tabula rasa, jointly with the policy and sometimes with auxiliary losses. This works for PointNav but gives weak results on semantic tasks: about 29.2% SR for single-RGB ImageNav and 18–24% for ObjectNav. Prior pretraining schemes for embodied agents either rely on agent-collected online data (CRL), on web image-text data (EmbCLIP/CLIP), or on temporal/pose signals.
motivation: As in 2D vision, representations matter. Self-supervised learning on large offline image collections is cheap and needs no labels, actions or pose, so the authors ask whether an offline-pretrained encoder, adapted during policy learning, beats in-vivo learning. A further question is whether the benefit survives long RL schedules, since pretraining gains often vanish with long finetuning (He et al.).
key_idea: Pretrain a ResNet50 encoder offline with DINO on ~14.5M pre-rendered indoor-scene images (Omnidata), then fine-tune it end-to-end with temporally consistent image augmentations inside the RL (ImageNav) or IL (ObjectNav) navigation policy.
insight: The source of the pretraining images matters most, not how many there are. On ImageNav SR, DINO on ImageNet-1k gives only 20.0 vs 17.9 from scratch; Gibson-ShortestPath gives 36.9 and OSD 41.3. OSD-10% (1.45M images) already matches the full set (41.2 vs 41.3), and ~60–600 images per scene suffice. Fine-tuning the encoder and augmentation are complementary (Table 4): augmentation hurts a frozen encoder (33.0→30.1 SR) but helps a fine-tuned one (35.3→41.3). SSL representations also generalize better than RL-learned ones (RL-pretrained encoders 27.3 SR vs 41.3), and the gap over scratch widens rather than shrinks over 2B frames on HM3D. DINO beats SimCLR (38.1) and MoCo-v2 (35.1), and ResNet50 beats ResNet18 (33.7); going larger brings little.
method: Offline SSL pretraining: DINO self-distillation (student matches EMA teacher; teacher centering and sharpening with τ_t=0.04, τ_s=0.1) with multi-crop (2×224² global + 8×96² local views); LARS, batch 8192, 100 epochs on 64 GPUs.

Encoder: ResNet50 with half width (32 baseplanes) and GroupNorm instead of BatchNorm (DD-PPO style); 3-layer MLP projection head (2048 hidden, K-dim weight-normed output) is discarded after pretraining.
Pretraining data: Omnidata Starter Dataset (~14.5M rendered images from Replica, Replica+GSO, Hypersim, Taskonomy, BlendedMVG, HM3D), excluding Gibson test scenes and CLEVR.

ImageNav policy: separate observation and goal encoders, both initialized from the pretrained ResNet50 and fine-tuned; features pass through FC layers, are concatenated with the previous action and fed to a 2-layer 512-d LSTM. Trained with DD-PPO for 500M steps; the 4-RGB variant sums per-camera goal features for rotation invariance. Optionally adds the ZER goal-view reward and goal-view sampling.

ObjectNav policy (built on Habitat-Web): pretrained RGB ResNet50 is fine-tuned; a frozen PointNav-pretrained depth ResNet50 is added. RGB and depth features plus GPS+Compass and goal-category embedding go into a 2-layer 2048-d GRU, trained with distributed behavior cloning on 40k human demos.

Augmentation: temporally consistent color jitter followed by random translation (ImageNav: jitter 0.3, pad 4; ObjectNav: jitter 0.4, pad 16), with separate augmentations for action sampling and for the update pass. Test-time augmentation is used for ImageNav results.

setting.backbone: ResNet50-32B (half-width, GroupNorm) pretrained with DINO on Omnidata, fine-tuned end-to-end with an LSTM policy (ImageNav, DD-PPO) or GRU policy (ObjectNav, behavior cloning; plus frozen PointNav-pretrained depth ResNet50)
setting.model_size: ResNet50 with 32 baseplanes visual encoder (parameter count not stated)
setting.training_data: DINO pretraining on Omnidata Starter Dataset (~14.5M rendered indoor images, Gibson test scenes excluded). ImageNav: DD-PPO RL for 500M steps on 72 Gibson train scenes (variant: 2B steps on 800 HM3D scenes with 8M PointNav episodes). ObjectNav: behavior cloning on 40k Habitat-Web human demonstrations (~13.7M frames) on MP3D train scenes, ~475M steps.
setting.observation: ImageNav: RGB only (128×128), 1 front camera or 4 cameras (front/back/left/right), plus goal image. ObjectNav: egocentric RGB-D + GPS/compass + goal category ID (also an RGB-only variant, with GPS/compass).
setting.action_space: low-level MOVE_FORWARD 0.25 m / TURN_LEFT/RIGHT 30° / STOP (ObjectNav adds LOOK_UP/LOOK_DOWN 30°)

numbers_note: ImageNav 'Test' is the 14 Gibson test scenes, evaluated with two episode sets: A (4,200 episodes from Mem-Aug RL) and B (3,000 episodes from NRNS). The paper notes ImageNav has no authoritative benchmark. The Gibson 1.5B-step OVRL run (SR 45.5, SPL 33.4, Table 7) and many ablations (dataset, SSL algorithm, model size, frozen/augmentation) are also on split A but are not listed. Training curves appear only in figures. The paper states the pretraining set is 14.5M images, but the compute section says 12 million.
results: On Gibson ImageNav with a single RGB camera, OVRL reaches 41.3% SR / 26.9% SPL vs 17.9% / 9.3% for an identical scratch agent. With the ZER reward added, it reaches 54.2% SR vs the prior best ZER at 29.2%. With 4 RGB cameras it gets 79.8% SR / 62.5% SPL vs Mem-Aug RL's 69.0% / 56.0%. On NRNS episodes it scores 45.5% SR vs NRNS's 24.0%, even though NRNS uses RGBD and pose. On MP3D ObjectNav test-std (RGBD), OVRL gets 23.2% SR / 7.6% SPL vs a re-implemented Habitat-Web at 17.9% / 6.1% and EmbCLIP at 18.1% SR, despite never seeing MP3D during pretraining. Its gains over scratch keep growing through 2B frames of HM3D training.
limitations: ObjectNav results are single-seed with very low SPL (~7%); in the RGB setting EmbCLIP still has higher SPL (7.8 vs 6.8), and the gain from pretraining shrinks once depth is added.

ImageNav numbers use test-time augmentation and custom episode splits (no standard benchmark), which complicates comparison; the approach is also compute-heavy (173 GPU-days pretraining, ~53 GPU-days per ImageNav run, >3500 GPU-days of analysis).
Only simulation (Habitat); no real-robot validation. Pretraining images are rendered from scene meshes that overlap with navigation datasets (HM3D, Taskonomy/Gibson train).
